existing_equivalents.finding: CanonicalASTRecord/ASTRecord is the datasets-owned, language-neutral, closed DAG-JSON AST/symbol IR. Records bind source CID, path, repository, revision, optional tree CID, byte/line/column SourceSpan, symbols, scopes, signatures, imports, unresolved references/calls, effects, diagnostics, and unsupported constructs. Content identity is software-contract-cid-profile-v1 CIDv1. References and calls carry no resolved target. This is the selected CanonicalCodeIR authority. The identifier CanonicalCodeIR@1 remains unregistered and absent from nested source.
existing_equivalents.reuse_decision: Select this schema as CanonicalCodeIR@1. Do not fork a second AST IR or add a proof_context wrapper.

existing_equivalents.finding: The frontend uses only ast.parse, never imports or executes analyzed source, and emits lexical facts into ASTRecord. Parse, encoding, and resource failures become diagnostics and UnsupportedConstruct records. python_frontend.ASTBlobRecord is an alias of ASTRecord. python_analysis projects frontend declarations into semantic-index symbols and classifies eval/exec/reflection/native/control-flow opacity; it does not emit a CFG or data-flow IR.
existing_equivalents.reuse_decision: Select as the Python v1 producer of CanonicalCodeIR. Do not treat opacity tags as CFG/data-flow.

existing_equivalents.finding: Projects ASTRecord into a closed asts catalog while preserving source CID, AST IR CID, and spans. Incompatible AST schema and identity drift fail closed. This is not a second AST schema.
existing_equivalents.reuse_decision: Reuse as a query projection. Do not treat the catalog as CanonicalCodeIR.
